The graph of the function $y=g(x)$ is shown above. 
Approximate $g'(x)$ at the point $x=4$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=4.$
examples.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
g'(x) \approx \dfrac{g(x+h) - g(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 

at the point $x=4$ with step size $h=4.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(4) & ≈\frac{g(4+4)-g(4-4)}{2(4)} \\  & =\frac{g(8)-g(0)}{8} \\  & =\frac{-4-(-10)}{8} \\  & =\frac{6}{8} \\  & =0.75.\end{aligned}
$$

Approximate ${g}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=-1$ using a central difference approximation.
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{g}^{′}(x)≈\frac{g(x+h)-g(x-h)}{2h}
$$

 
at the point $x=-1.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=0.05.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(-1) & ≈\frac{g(-1+0.05)-g(-1-0.05)}{2(0.05)} \\  & =\frac{g(-0.95)-g(-1.05)}{2(0.05)} \\  & =\frac{1.6-3.4}{0.1} \\  & =\frac{-1.8}{0.1} \\  & =\frac{-18}{1} \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$
